items.topic: Does "Show anyway" gate graph rendering, or is it just a labeled dismiss?
items.context: Today the graph always renders; the high-edge banner is a non-blocking suggestion that can be dismissed with ×. The item description says "render the graph regardless," which implies a possible new gating: hide the graph until the user opts in. This is the highest-impact decision because it changes default behavior for every user who hits >500 edges.

options.label: Non-gating: keep current behavior, rename × to a "Show anyway" button (acknowledge + hide warning)
options.rationale: Smallest behavior change. Graph still renders by default. "Show anyway" just acknowledges the warning and dismisses the banner. Lowest regression risk.

options.label: Gating: when edges > threshold, hide graph behind a centered warning card with "Show anyway" as the primary action
options.rationale: Matches the literal reading of "bypass the performance warning and render the graph regardless." Protects users from accidental slow renders. Bigger UX shift — every large-graph user now clicks a button per session.

options.label: Soft-gate: render graph but with reduced fidelity (e.g., hide secondary edges) until "Show anyway" is clicked
options.rationale: Compromise — gives partial value immediately and full fidelity on opt-in. More implementation work; needs a clear definition of "reduced fidelity".

items.context: Once a user clicks "Show anyway," how long does it last? Currently the dismiss × is component-local state that auto-resets when edge count drops below 500 (lines 352-356).

options.label: Session-scoped, auto-reset when edges drop below threshold (current pattern, applied to Show anyway)
options.rationale: Consistent with existing dismiss behavior. Banner re-appears on a future spike, which is desirable as a fresh signal.

options.label: Sticky for the tab session — once acknowledged, never re-appears until reload
options.rationale: Less interruptive for power users who already know their graph is large. Loses the "this just spiked" signal.

options.label: Persisted across sessions (localStorage)
options.rationale: Most user-friendly, but easy to forget the warning ever existed. Hard to surface again if behavior regresses.

items.topic: Which overlays count as "informational/status" and should be recentered?
items.context: GraphCanvas.tsx has six overlays. Two are already centered (graph-empty, FocusEmptyState). Four are scattered: graph-loading (top-14), graph-error (top-14), filter-suggestion (top-24), operations-agent-manager-warning (bottom-3 left-3). The description says "All informational/status overlays" — needs a concrete list.

options.label: Recenter all four scattered overlays (loading, error, filter-suggestion, agent-manager-unavailable)
options.rationale: Most literal interpretation of "all" in the description. Uniform pattern across the canvas.

options.label: Recenter only the three top-edge banners (loading, error, filter-suggestion); leave agent-manager-unavailable in its bottom-left corner
options.rationale: Agent-manager-unavailable is a persistent low-priority status flag, not a blocking alert — corner placement is conventional for that. Keeps it out of the way of graph interaction.

options.label: Recenter only the filter-suggestion (the warning explicitly mentioned in the title); leave others alone
options.rationale: Minimal change, lowest risk of unintended UX shifts. But contradicts the "all" wording in the description.

items.topic: Stacking strategy when multiple centered overlays would be visible at once
items.context: Centering all overlays on the same `top-1/2 left-1/2` point causes z-axis overlap when, e.g., the graph is loading AND has too many edges AND agent-manager is unavailable. Need a strategy.

options.label: Priority-based: show only the highest-priority overlay (error > gating warning > loading > non-gating warnings)
options.rationale: Cleanest visual; user always sees one card. Hides simultaneous status — but in practice that is rarely useful information at the same instant.

options.label: Vertical stack inside a single centered container (cards stacked with gap)
options.rationale: Shows everything at once without overlap. Centered group can grow tall — risk of overflowing the canvas height when many overlays appear.

options.label: Suppress non-error overlays while loading; otherwise stack vertically
options.rationale: Hybrid: hides the chatter during loading, reveals all once stable. Slightly more state.

items.topic: Extract a shared GraphOverlayCard component vs inline the centered shell
items.context: The same Tailwind shell (absolute centered, rounded card, shadow, semantic color) will be reused across overlays. Worth extracting?

options.label: Extract `GraphOverlayCard` with a `tone` prop (info | warning | error | neutral) for consistent styling
options.rationale: DRY, easy to keep all overlays visually consistent, and gives tests a single render target. Small additional file is justified by 4-5 call sites.

options.label: Inline the shell at each overlay site with shared Tailwind classes via a `clsx` helper
options.rationale: Less indirection. But duplicated structure across 4-5 sites drifts over time.

items.text: FocusEmptyState shell pattern (the centering reference): `absolute left-1/2 top-1/2 z-10 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2` with a `rounded-2xl border bg-slate-950/95 px-6 py-5 shadow-xl text-center` card. The high-edge threshold is `FILTER_SUGGESTION_THRESHOLD = 500` in `surfaces/graph/lib/edge-styles.ts:115`. Today the graph always renders past the threshold; the banner is purely advisory. Set acceptance_allow to `scenarios/swarm-manager/ui/src/surfaces/graph/**`.
